answer: Imagine two ships sailing toward one horizon, each holding a sonnet whose fourteen lines are locked in order, each line sealed by the one before it. The bond stays locked until five strangers on distant shores re-attest every line. A hollow copy earns nothing: re-attestation reads the cargo, not the cover. One honest ship passes with 90% odds; ten copies pass together only 35% of the time, yet the fleet pays ten bonds. I sail one ship and earn what its own lines earned.
